content_preview.title: DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS Ships Triggers, a Default PEG Parser and Asynchronous I/O, and Older Versions Cannot Read Its Database Files
content_preview.summary: DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS, released October 21, adds triggers, the Quack CONNECT statement, a PEG parser and async I/O; versions before 2.0 cannot read files it creates.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The DuckDB team released DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS on October 21, 2026, according to its [announcement post](https://duckdb.org/2026/10/21/announcing-duckdb-200.html). The release is codenamed "Cinnamon Teal" and, in the team's words, is "our biggest feature release so far," built from close to 20,000 commits since DuckDB 1.5. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (781 words, range 400-1200): overview, support windows, feature list, migration, context, and an explicit 'What We Don't Know' section. Precise and neutral.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk (gunzip, text-extracted) and re-fetched both live URLs; live text matched snapshots. manifest suspicious_patterns null for both. source-0.html.gz (duckdb.org announcement, dated 2026-10-21, codename 'Cinnamon Teal' (Spatula cyanoptera)): confirmed 'biggest feature release so far' and 'close to 20,000 commits since DuckDB 1.5'; the '1.0 was all about stability and backward compatibility, DuckDB 2.0 is above all a feature release' quote verbatim; LTS 'with support until at least October 2027'; 1.4 supported until November 17, 2026; 1.5 extended to March 2027 'effectively also turning it into an LTS release'; Quack polished, CONNECT statement, works with any remote DB that supports it incl. PostgreSQL and MySQL, remote pushdown optimizer, localhost-only default; async I/O for Parquet, CSV and native storage with 'dramatically faster queries on object storage such as s3://' verbatim (article's trailing period sits inside the quote marks, trivial); VARIANT from 1.5 now fully integrated with shredding and Parquet read/write; PEG parser debuted opt-in in 1.5, now default, replaces PostgreSQL-derived parser, revert via SET enable_legacy_parser = true with legacy_parser extension; triggers: CREATE TRIGGER, BEFORE/AFTER, FOR EACH ROW/STATEMENT, REFERENCING OLD/NEW TABLE, with BEFORE...FOR EACH ROW and UPDATE...FOR EACH ROW not yet supported; SQL additions list matches; agent mode 59% on TPC-H; 'a small set of breaking changes' verbatim; storage statement 'DuckDB versions before 2.0 cannot read database files created by DuckDB 2.0. DuckDB 2.0 can still read and write your existing database files, and these remain readable by older versions' (direction: forward-incompatible only for files created by 2.0; 2.0 reads old files; no export/migration path is given beyond the migration guide, and the article does not claim one); 'first patch release, coming in November' verbatim; C++17, ICU removed with ~45 kB tz data, single-arrow lambda disabled and removed in v2.1, amalgamation deprecated, osx_amd64 dropped in 2.1 with community extensions no longer built; extension repositories 'work in progress' with syntax possibly changing. source-1.html.gz (GitHub release page): title 'DuckDB v2.0.0 "Cyanoptera"', released 21 Oct 12:49, datetime attribute 2026-10-21T12:49:12Z, confirms the 12:49 UTC claim; states 'named "Cyanoptera" after Spatula Cyanoptera'. The GitHub page does not itself state LTS or storage compatibility; the article attributes those only to the announcement. Allowlist: duckdb.org and github.com both present in config/source_allowlist.txt. No orphan URLs: the only external body URLs are the two sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, quote and attribution checked individually and traced to the cited sources. Codename: the blog uses 'Cinnamon Teal' and the GitHub title uses 'Cyanoptera' (the species name, Spatula cyanoptera, which the blog also mentions). The article uses the blog's codename and attributes it to the announcement; not misleading, though it does not mention the GitHub 'Cyanoptera' title, which the August preview piece used as the codename. Headline phrase 'Older Versions Cannot Read Its Database Files' compresses 'files created by DuckDB 2.0'; the body states the exact scope and that 2.0 reads existing files that stay readable by older versions, so the nuance is preserved. No unsupported 'first'/'only' superlatives (the 'first' in the linked Aurora article's title belongs to that earlier piece, which attributes it to InfoQ). Internal links all use /article/<YYYY-MM>/<slug>, files exist, and descriptions match: Aug 20 preview (PEG grammar), Aug 26 AWS agreement to acquire DuckLabs (article says 'signing an agreement', consistent with the Aurora piece noting no closing date), Oct 19 Vera benchmark of the v2.0 preview, Oct 21 Aurora embedding DuckDB, Oct 14 agent mode in the unreleased CLI.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, factual, no editorializing and no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New event (the actual release) with a distinct angle from the earlier preview, agent-mode, benchmark and Aurora articles, which are linked as prior coverage rather than repeated.
concerns: Both sources are first-party (DuckDB project); no independent coverage was found, which the article discloses explicitly.
Codename divergence between the blog (Cinnamon Teal) and GitHub title (Cyanoptera) is not mentioned in the article; low-impact.
recommendations: Mention both codenames when they differ across first-party pages.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped release coverage with a clear compatibility warning and honest limitations; all claims verified against raw text of both sources. Featured candidacy: 2 - DuckDB 2.0 LTS is a major release of a widely used database with a one-way storage-format change affecting a broad developer audience
